items.title: The spring tokens' linear() curves jump to 1 in their last stop
items.dedupe_of: O-311 (INBOUND.md:286; animation AUDIT.md:178 row 2), booked to 11.1.2 by glass-11.1.1-scope.md:1 and :81. The intake row for this relay is O-416 (INBOUND.md:406, master b7b6a3192).
items.evidence: Tokens: src/styles/tokens/scheme-spring.css:59-64. The file is byte-identical on v11.1.0, master and the tip d0f85bd29. git diff v11.1.0..master and v11.1.0..d0f85bd29 is empty for scheme-spring.css, springProjection.ts, springPresets.ts and regen-spring-tokens.mjs, and git log --all since 2026-11-09 finds no commit on any of them. The stops are generated. scripts/regen-spring-tokens.mjs:45-58 reads springProjection(preset).stops. springProjection.ts:48-68 calls springLinearStops with maxDuration set to the row's numeric settle (:51-55, :64). springLinearStops (keyframes src/animation/physics/spring/css/linear-stops.ts:54-70, and the same code in glass's installed 6.0.0 at dist/sequence-BvpIpCGp.js:476-490) samples at i*T/49 for i = 1..48, then pins the last stop with push("1") (:69). The JS twin pins the same way (timing-function.ts:75-76). Recomputed here: the analytic step response (omega = 2*pi/response, keyframes progress.ts:157) matches every shipped stop to within its 5-decimal rounding (max error 5.0e-6). v(T): press 0.98089, present 0.97781, dock 0.97677, panel 1.00470, bloom 0.99568, world 0.99514. Speed of the last segment over the one before, from the shipped stops: press 4.31x, present 9.65x, dock 6.72x (0.97317 at 97.959 %, then 1), panel 3.88x (a 0.61 % fall from above 1), bloom 3.76x, world 6.95x. All six match the relay's numbers. --transition-liquid-spatial aliases --spring-press (:142). Consumer: keyframes .worktrees/o41-keyframes @ 5c8a7c55, demo/components/instrument/transport/AnimationControlsGroup.css:229-230 and :247, runs translate and scale on var(--spring-dock-duration) var(--spring-dock). That is a 210 ms clock, so the last segment lasts 4.3 ms and carries 0.0268 x 280 px = 7.5 px, matching the probe's 7.64 px -> 2.63 px -> none (PR-BODY.md:110). Header citations, corrected: the 'sub-perceptual' wording is only in regen-spring-tokens.mjs:117-119. scheme-spring.css:86-89 claims instead that the numeric horizon removed the endpoint snap. Both conflict with LAW 0b (:30-33).
items.cure: Root cause: the curve is sampled up to the settle horizon, where the spring is still 2.3 to 2.7 % short of 1 (0.4 to 0.5 % on the 0.005-band rows; panel is 0.47 % over). The last stop is then pinned to 1, so the whole residual closes in one 1/49 segment. Smallest cure, in glass and not in the keyframes package (keyframes' default 4x-response horizon leaves a residual near 1e-10; glass's short horizon is what exposes the pin): in springProjection.ts:48-68, take v(T) from SpringProgress.tickToTime(settleSeconds) (the call :35-41 already makes) and divide every interior value by it, keeping the final 1. keyframes 6.0.0 exports only springLinearStops and springTimingFunction, both pinned, so glass rescales the interior values itself, both in the string at :64 and in the timing function and peak at :56-60 (the last LUT segment must lerp to 1, not to 1/v(T)). Then rerun regen-spring-tokens.mjs. Divide by v(T), not by the last interior sample as AUDIT.md:178 words it (INBOUND O-311 already says the value at settle time). Names and clocks do not change. Cured last-to-previous ratios: press 0.91, present 0.91, dock 0.90, panel 0.89, bloom 0.86, world 0.88. Panel's peak goes from +4.2 % to +3.7 %, the mirror line regenerates, and LAW 0 holds. Correction to the earlier figure: t90 moves earlier on five rows (press 94.9 -> 91.4 ms, present 136.2 -> 128.2, dock 158.3 -> 150.2, bloom 227.7 -> 225.3, world 297.3 -> 293.1) and 1.3 ms later on panel (169.7 -> 171.0, because v(T) > 1 shrinks it). The 'CSS_t90 == JS_t90' lines (:79-80, :93-95) need restating. Witness: a static vitest over each --spring-* linear() in scheme-spring.css, requiring the last segment's slope to be at most 1.5x the previous segment's, with the same sign. RED on v11.1.0 for all six (4.31, 9.65, 6.72, 3.88, 3.76, 6.95), GREEN after. springProjection.test.ts:24-44 stays GREEN after the regen, provided the peak comes from the normalized timing function. keyframes' unchanged pane-slide at 120 Hz is the consumer's witness.
items.row: K1 is O-311, already booked: the cure in springProjection.ts plus a regen, witnessed by a 1.5x bound on each token's last segment. It was first placed for 11.1.1, and the exits order (O-365) moved it to 11.1.2 (scope :1, :81). The tip has not touched it. It is not an exits row. The only exit that pairs a spring curve on the tip is sortable-list/styles.css:226, an opacity leg and not a surface that opens. The fix corrects a token value to its stated intent ('dead landing'), so it is a patch. K1 adds a consumer witness: keyframes' pane-slide at 120 Hz, a 280 px stroke on --spring-dock. It also adds cure details: divide by v(T); glass rescales the stops itself, since keyframes' exports pin the last stop; regenerate panel's mirror line to +3.7 %; restate the t90 parity line, noting that panel moves 1.3 ms later.
items.reply: Confirmed, and all six spring curves have it, not only dock, present and press. Each curve is sampled up to the moment the spring settles, when it is still 2.3 to 2.7 % short of the end on the three fast curves and about half a percent off on the three long ones, and the last stop then jumps straight to 1. glass 11.1.2 regenerates all six so each one reaches 1 on its own slope, with the same names and durations; the fast curves reach 90 % a few milliseconds sooner. Your pane-slide check should pass with no change on your side.

items.title: A tooltip opens on the focus a closing Sheet or Dialog hands back to its opener
items.dedupe_of: O-350(9) (INBOUND.md:329), booked to 11.1.2 at glass-11.1.1-scope.md:96 and :179. Same object as atlas G13 (O-413), triage-1119/PLACED.md:9.
items.evidence: glass moves focus back to the opener in two places, and only the second can be cancelled by a consumer. (1) The focus handoff: a flush-sync watch on the logical close focuses the trigger whenever the active element is inside the closing content. On v11.1.0 and master it is at DialogContent.vue:133-142 (focus at :139) and SheetContent.vue:265-274 (:271); on the tip at DialogContent.vue:141-150 (:147) and SheetContent.vue:285-294 (:291). This is the path the relay describes ('when it closes on a focus inside it'). (2) returnFocusQuietly on reka's close-auto-focus (_shared/overlay/focus-return.ts:9-14, the same on both trees), wired at DialogContent.vue:143,204 and SheetContent.vue:275,316 on v11.1.0 and master, and at DialogContent.vue:151,244 and SheetContent.vue:295,365 on the tip. Neither Sheet nor Dialog handles open-auto-focus, so reka also focuses into the surface by script when it opens. keyframes needed two workarounds to match: a blur inside the sheet before the close, for path 1 (ControlsPaneWrapper.vue:727-730), and preventDefault on close-auto-focus after a touch, for path 2 (:833-835), in .worktrees/o41-keyframes @ 5c8a7c55. Opening on focus is reka-ui 2.10.1's behaviour (lock 2.10.1). In TooltipTrigger.js:70-74, handleFocus returns only while the trigger's own pointer is down (:71), or when ignoreNonKeyboardFocus is set and the target does not match :focus-visible (:72). Otherwise it opens at once (TooltipRoot.js:82-86). Only the hover path checks pointer type (:60). ignoreNonKeyboardFocus defaults to false (TooltipProvider.js:35-39; the root inherits it, TooltipRoot.js:44-48,60). glass dropped the passthrough in 7.0.0 (490cc46e3): Tooltip.vue:29-36 binds only open, defaultOpen, delayDuration and disabled, with inheritAttrs false (:18), and TooltipProvider.vue:21-24 binds only the two delays. Tests pin that: tooltip.contract.test.ts:128-180 asserts that the root's ignoreNonKeyboardFocus is undefined (:174), and floating.public-contracts.test-d.ts:76 asserts that TooltipProps lacks it. Tooltip.vue, TooltipTrigger.vue and TooltipProvider.vue are unchanged across v11.1.0, master and the tip. The tip changes only TooltipContent.vue (leave-finished), and no branch changes these files after 2026-11-09.
items.cure: Root cause: the tooltip has no keyboard-focus check. reka ships one (ignoreNonKeyboardFocus, a :focus-visible test), but it is off by default and glass's Tooltip leaves it off. So every scripted focus, from either return path above, opens the hint at once. A coarse-pointer check would be the wrong fix: it would leave a mouse-closed dialog raising the tooltip, and it would hide a real keyboard focus on a touch device that has a keyboard. Smallest cure: Tooltip.vue:29-36 passes :ignore-non-keyboard-focus="true" to RekaTooltipRoot. No prop is added (the d.ts test at :76 stays), and no consumer could choose the old value through glass, so it is a patch. The cure also updates tooltip.contract.test.ts: the assertion at :174 flips to true, and the two tests that open the tooltip with a synthetic focus event (:77-87, :104-126) must really focus the trigger. happy-dom matches :focus-visible on any active element (SelectorItem.js:341-345), so the scripted-return case can only be shown in a browser. Witness, in Chromium and WebKit at 390 with hasTouch: a Sheet and a Dialog whose trigger sits inside TooltipTrigger as-child. Open each by tap and close it three ways: tap Close, swipe the sheet down, and a scripted close. After each, focus is on the opener and no [role=tooltip] mounts within 1000 ms. Repeat with a mouse-click close at 1440. Tab onto the opener, and a close by Escape, still open the tooltip. RED on v11.1.0, GREEN after. The WebKit swipe leg matters because engines differ on :focus-visible after a scripted focus. Chromium carries the state forward from the previous focus. WebKit, as I recall its rule (unverified here), looks only at whether the last focus came from a click, so reka's scripted focus on open followed by the scripted return can match :focus-visible there. If that leg stays RED, the fix moves to the two returns glass owns (path 1 and path 2 above): after a pointer close they ask for a focus that is not visible (FocusOptions.focusVisible: false, once engine support is checked). It does not move to a pointer-type check.
items.row: K2 is O-350(9), already booked: a Tooltip opens on a pointer move or a keyboard focus only, never on a programmatic focus return. It was placed for 11.1.1, but the exits patch did not build it. Exits row 6 covers only the tooltip's enter and leave tweens, and row 8 only O-350's reduced-motion part. It sits in 11.1.2's scope at :96 and :179, and triage-1119 ruled its cure for atlas G13: reka's ignoreNonKeyboardFocus set inside glass's Tooltip. K2 narrows the ask to a coarse pointer, but the root is the missing :focus-visible check, not pointer type. K2 adds to the row: glass's second return path (the logical-close handoff, which a consumer cannot cancel); the three contract tests the cure must update; and a WebKit swipe-dismiss leg in the witness, with the fallback at glass's own focus returns if WebKit marks the returned focus visible. Exposing the option as a prop stays 11.3.0, if anyone still needs it.
items.reply: Confirmed: glass's Tooltip opens on any focus, including the one a closing Sheet or Dialog hands back to its opener, because the tooltip's keyboard-focus check is left off. glass 11.1.2 turns that check on inside Tooltip, so a focus handed back after a tap, a click or a swipe raises no tooltip, while Tab and a close by Escape still show it. We will check it in Safari's engine, swipe-down close included, before we suggest you drop the touch-close workaround.

changed: K1: verdict and release kept. Corrected three statements in the evidence and cure. (a) t90 moves earlier on five rows but 1.3 ms later on panel (169.7 -> 171.0 ms, because v(T) = 1.0047 > 1); the placement said all rows move 1-8 ms earlier. (b) The analytic match is within the stops' 5-decimal rounding (max 5.0e-6), not 1.4e-5. (c) The 'sub-perceptual' wording is only in regen-spring-tokens.mjs:117-119; scheme-spring.css:86-89 claims the numeric horizon removed the snap. Added that keyframes 6.0.0 exports only springLinearStops and springTimingFunction, both pinned, so glass must rescale the interior values itself (and lerp the last LUT segment to 1). Added the O-416 intake row. Reply notes the fast curves reach 90 % a few ms sooner.

K2: verdict and release kept. Evidence now names glass's second focus return, the logical-close handoff watch (DialogContent.vue:133-142 / SheetContent.vue:265-274 on v11.1.0 and master; :141-150 / :285-294 on the tip), which a consumer's close-auto-focus preventDefault cannot cancel; it is why keyframes also blurs at :727-730. Added the 7.0.0 removal of the passthrough (490cc46e3) and the tests the cure must update (tooltip.contract.test.ts:174 flips to true; the synthetic-focus tests at :77-87 and :104-126 must really focus the trigger; happy-dom treats any active element as :focus-visible). Added a WebKit swipe-dismiss leg to the witness, because WebKit's script-focus rule may mark the returned focus visible, with the fallback at glass's own focus returns (focusVisible: false after a pointer close). The reply no longer promises keyframes can drop its workaround until the Safari-engine check passes.
